blocks.task_summary: Show that θ = 2.08 radians (3 s.f.) by equating the total sheet-metal width 45 cm to twice the vertical side 10 cm plus the arc length, then using arc length = rθ with r = 12 cm.

evidence.basis: recognition that 45 = 10 + 10 + arc length (M1); arc length = 25 (cm) (A1); 25 = 12θ, θ = 2.08 correct to 3 significant figures AG (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Find the cross-sectional area of the gutter by first determining the width w (via cosine rule, sine rule, or right-triangle trigonometry with θ/2), then computing the area as (sector OAB − triangle OAB + rectangle CDBA) or as (2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB), giving approximately 294 cm².
accepted_alternatives: Use sine rule 12/sin(θ) = w/sin(π−θ)/2 to find w
Use right-triangle trig with angle θ/2 and hypotenuse 12 to find w/2
Area via 2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB
Area via rectangle CDFE + 2 × triangle EOA + sector OAB

evidence.basis: First three marks for finding w: evidence of using cosine rule OR sine rule (M1); w² = 12²+12²−2·12·12·cos(2.08) OR 12/sin(2.08) = w/sin(0.530796...) (A1); w ≈ 20.6977 or w/2 ≈ 10.3488 (A1). OR using trig ratios in right triangle with angle 2.08/2 and side w/2 (M1); sin(2.08/2) = (w/2)/12 (A1); w ≈ 20.6977 (A1).

(segment AHB =) sector OAB − triangle OAB (M1); = ½·12²·2.08 − ½·12²·sin(2.08) = 149.76 − 62.8655... = 86.8944... (A1); valid approach to find total cross-sectional area (M1); sector OAB − triangle OAB + rectangle CDBA = 86.8944... + 10w = 86.8944... + 206.977... (A1 for final area 294 cm²).

OR trapezium CGOA approach: trapezium CGOA (M1); = ½(20.6977... + 10 + 10 − 12cos(1.04)) × 10 ≈ 72.0557 (A1); valid approach to total area (M1); 2 × trapezium CGOA + sector OAB = 2(72.0557...) + ½·12²·2.08 = 144.111... + 149.76 (A1 for final 294 cm²).

blocks.task_summary: Determine whether the gutter overflows by computing gutter volume (600 × cross-sectional area ≈ 176,323–176,658 cm³) and comparing with the total rainfall over 60 seconds, given R′(t) = 50 cos(2πt/5) + 3000. The rainfall ∫₀⁶⁰ R′(t) dt = 180,000 cm³ exceeds the gutter volume, so it overflows.
accepted_alternatives: Use minimum of R′(t) = 2950 cm³/s to bound rainfall from below: 60 × 2950 = 177,000 > gutter volume
Solve ∫₀ᵀ R′(t) dt = gutter volume to find T ≈ 58.8 s < 60 s

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: volume of gutter = 176323 OR 176658 (OR 600×their area) (A1); recognising rainfall can be represented by an integral (M1); ∫₀⁶⁰ R′(t) dt (A1); rainfall over 60 seconds = 180000 (cm³) (A1); the gutter will overflow because the rainfall > gutter volume (A1).

METHOD 2 (alternative): volume of gutter (A1); recognition that cosine has a minimum value of −1 (M1); R′(t) ≥ −1×50 + 3000 = 2950 cm³/s (A1); rainfall over 60 seconds ≥ 177000 (A1); overflow because rainfall > gutter volume (A1).

METHOD 3 (alternative): volume of gutter (A1); recognising rainfall as integral (M1); attempt to solve 60 > 58.8 OR ∫₀ᵀ R′(t) dt = 176658 (M1); time to reach overflow = 58.7875... or 58.8990... (A1); gutter overflows because 60 > 58.8 or 60 > 58.9 (A1).
